station]] }} The '''Dhaka Metro Rail''' ({{lang-bn|ঢাকা মেট্রোরেল}}), colloquially known as the '''Dhaka Metro''' ({{lang-bn|ঢাকা মেট্রো}}) is a [[Rapid transit|mass rapid transit]] (MRT) system serving [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]]. Together with the city's proposed [[Dhaka Subway|subway system]], it is expected to reduce [[Traffic congestion|congestion]] in the capital. It is part of the 20-year long Strategic Transport Plan (STP) outlined by the [[Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority|Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA)]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.dmtc.org.bd/about/about-mrt-line-6|title=About MRT Line-6|website=DHAKA MASS TRANSIT COMPANY LTD.|publisher=DHAKA MASS TRANSIT COMPANY LTD.|access-date=28 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202061003/http://www.dmtc.org.bd/about/about-mrt-line-6|archive-date=2 February 2017|url-status=dead}} The first phase of Dhaka Metro's [[MRT Line 6]] commenced commercial operations on 28 December 2022, after being inaugurated by [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Prime Minister]] Sheikh Hasina, with metro services being available to general commuters the next day.{{cite web | url=https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-becomes-first-passenger-travel-metro-rail-ticket-559082 | title=PM Hasina becomes first passenger to travel on Metro Rail with ticket | date=28 December 2022 }}{{Cite web |author=Staff Correspondent |title=Passengers gather at Dhaka metro stations at first light |url=https://bdnews24.com/metro-rail/o2sjvoesf1 |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=bdnews24.com |language=en}} The construction of MRT Line 6's second phase is scheduled to be completed by 2023.{{Cite web |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/transport/metro-magic-here-now-558862 |title=Metro magic is here, now |date=2022-12-27 |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=[[The Business Standard]] |last=Datta Gupta |first=Titu |archive-url=https://archive.ph/fNyZF |archive-date=2022-12-29 |url-status=live}} The third phase will contain an additional 1.16 km extension at [[Kamalapur railway station]] which will have an [[Interchange station|interchange]] with [[MRT Line 1 (Dhaka Metro)|MRT Line 1]], MRT Line 2 and MRT Line 4 and is set to be completed by 2025.{{Cite web |author=Staff Correspondent |date=2021-12-13 |title=Metro Rail: Roll-out on Victory Day next year |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/transport/news/metro-rail-roll-out-victory-day-next-year-2915931 |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=The Daily Star |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=হোসেন |first=আনোয়ার |title=প্রযুক্তির চমক মেট্রোরেলে |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/technology/e5t9zoe6r2 |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=Prothomalo |language=bn}}{{Cite web |title=Redirect Notice |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/underground-metro-tunnels-run-deep-22-storeys-3235721 |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=www.google.com|date=February 2023 }} The network is planned to contain six lines. Of these, two are under construction, with the rest still in the planning stages. == History == In an effort to implement Dhaka's 20-year-long Strategic Transport Plan (STP), the [[Government of Bangladesh]] invited the [[Japan International Cooperation Agency]] (JICA) to conduct a primary survey and feasibility study on the transport system of Dhaka in 2009–2010. In 2012, the Government's Executive Committee of National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved the project. A loan agreement between the Bangladeshi government and JICA was signed in January 2013. Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTC), the agency responsible for the implementation of the first metro line (MRT Line-6) was formed in January 2013. The General Consultant (GC), namely the NKDM Association, commenced work beginning in February 2014. In June 2013, Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTC) was established by the Government to implement the Metro Rail Lines across the city.{{Cite web |title=About DMTC Line 6- The Official Website for the Dhaka MRT Project |url=http://www.dmtc.org.bd/about/about-dmtc |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202060651/http://www.dmtc.org.bd/about/about-dmtc |archive-date=2 February 2017 |access-date=28 January 2017 |website=DHAKA MASS TRANSIT COMPANY LTD. |publisher=DHAKA MASS TRANSIT COMPANY LTD.}} === History of MRT Line-6 === ==== Construction ==== [[File:Dhaka Metro Rail Project.jpg|thumb|Line-6 under construction in 2020]] The deal for construction of the MRT Line-6, costing US$2.8 billion, was signed by the [[Government of Bangladesh]] with the [[Japan International Cooperation Agency]] on 20 February 2013.{{cite news |url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/afp/130220/bangladesh-japan-strike-deal-28-bln-dhaka-metro-rail-0 |title=Bangladesh, Japan strike deal for $2.81-bln Dhaka metro rail |newspaper=GlobalPost |date=20 February 2013 |access-date=21 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130521135029/http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/afp/130220/bangladesh-japan-strike-deal-28-bln-dhaka-metro-rail-0 |archive-date=21 May 2013 }} Construction began on 26 June 2016 with an inauguration ceremony presided over by the prime minister [[Sheikh Hasina]].{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/pm-opens-work-metro-brt-1246204|title=PM opens work on metro, BRT|newspaper=The Daily Star|date=27 June 2016|access-date=25 July 2016|archive-date=7 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807111652/http://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/pm-opens-work-metro-brt-1246204|url-status=live}} Civil engineering work was done by the [[Italian-Thai Development]] Public Company Ltd. and China's Sinohydro Corporation Ltd. JV, and a Tokyo-based construction company developed the depot's land.{{cite news|date=12 October 2017|title=Just 12% progress made in metro rail project in 4 years|publisher=Dhaka Tribune|url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/development/2017/10/12/just-12-progress-made-metro-rail-project-4-years/|url-status=live|access-date=26 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227153454/http://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/development/2017/10/12/just-12-progress-made-metro-rail-project-4-years/|archive-date=27 February 2018}}{{cite web|title=Building Bangladesh's first Mass Rapid Transit System|url=https://www.lntecc.com/projects/metros/dhaka-metro/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802204959/https://www.lntecc.com/projects/metros/dhaka-metro/|archive-date=2 August 2021|access-date=3 August 2021}} Construction work was divided into eight packages, covering aspects like depots, stations and rolling stock.{{cite web |title=Document MRT Line-6 |url=http://dmtcl.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/dmtcl.portal.gov.bd/page/1e55ee49_2891_4c82_b439_1e81df4d6cf7/2022-11-06-06-13-3c264a15cbaa05ecc5475d569df027fc.pdf |access-date=29 November 2022}} ====Planning==== When construction started in 2016, opening was expected by the end of 2019.{{r|"TDS-June28"}} By 2018, this expectation was still held to, but by 2019, completion of phase one was delayed to December 2021.{{cite news |last1=Report |first1=Star Online |title=Fact box: All you need to know about metro rail project |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/country/dhaka-metro-rail-project-in-bangladesh-fact-box-all-you-need-to-know-about-this-1569868 |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=The Daily Star |date=30 April 2018 |language=en}} In 2018, the second phase was expected to be complete by December 2020.{{cite news |last1=Report |first1=Star Online |title=Metro rail service delayed by 1yr, to be launched Dec 2021 |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/city/news/metro-rail-service-delayed-1yr-be-launched-dec-2021-1750543 |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=The Daily Star |date=29 May 2019 |language=en}} Eventually, these dates were pushed back, with phase one opening in 2022 and phase two expected in 2023.{{cite news |last1=Express |first1=The Financial |title=Dhaka metro-rail travel turning real |url=https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/views/dhaka-metro-rail-travel-turning-real-1662996280 |access-date=4 December 2022 |work=The Financial Express |language=en}} The main reason for the delays from 2020 to 2022 was the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news |last1=Ahmed |first1=Zafar |title=Metro rail, first in Bangladesh, was delayed by COVID-19. A new date is far off |url=https://bdnews24.com/economy/metro-rail-first-in-bangladesh-was-delayed-by-covid-19.-a-new-date-is-far-off |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=bdnews24.com |language=en}} ==== Cost and length changes ==== Originally, the project cost was Tk 21,985 crore but it was later increased by Tk 11,487 to Tk 33,472 crore. The first route, originally projected to start from [[Uttara (Town)|Uttara]], a northern area of Dhaka, to Sayedabad, in the south of the capital,{{cite news|url=http://www.thefinancialexpress-bd.com/more.php?news_id=140486&date=2011-06-25|title=Muhith to sit with armed forces to resolve metro rail site dispute|newspaper=The Financial Express|date=25 June 2011|access-date=25 June 2011|archive-date=29 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629162724/http://www.thefinancialexpress-bd.com/more.php?news_id=140486&date=2011-06-25|url-status=live}} was eventually extended north to Uttara and truncated south to Motijheel.{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/37-minutes-1245778|title=In 37 minutes|date=26 June 2016|access-date=25 July 2016|archive-date=16 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160716004148/http://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/37-minutes-1245778|url-status=live}} The original length which was {{convert|20.10|km|mi|abbr=on}} has been increased by 1.16 km to {{convert|21.26|km|mi|abbr=on}}. It was planned to have 16 stations originally but it has been increased to 17 stations.{{cite news |last1=Adhikary |first1=Tuhin Shubhra |last2=Byron |first2=Rejaul Karim |title=Dhaka Metro Rail now set to cost 50% more |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/transport/news/metro-now-set-cost-50pc-more-3072816 |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=The Daily Star |date=18 July 2022 |language=en}} ==== Misconceptions ==== The project was originally reported to be a {{convert|27|km|mi|abbr=on}} underground metro rail line. It was later confirmed to be an elevated and underground metro rail project.{{cite news |title=Dhaka Metro likely by 2013 |url=https://dhakamirror.com/news/other-headlines/dhaka-metro-likely-by-2013/ |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=Dhaka Mirror |date=28 May 2010}} In 2014, it was reported that 56 trains would run on the metro system.{{cite news |last1=Ahmed |first1=Shamim |title=Dhaka Metrorail to carry 60,000 people per hour |url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/dhaka-metrorail-to-carry-60000-people-per-hour |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=bdnews24.com |language=en}} It was confirmed that 24 vehicles would run on the MRT Line-6. It was planned to have six lines. ==== Trial runs ==== MRT Line-6's train made its first run on 29 August 2021. It traveled from Diabari Depot to Mirpur 12. It successfully made its second run on 29 November 2021. It traveled from Uttara to Mirpur 10. The line's train made its longest trial run on 12 December 2021. It traveled from Uttara to Agargaon. The train ran for {{convert|11.3|km|mi|abbr=on}}. It ran at 100 km/h for {{convert|9|km|mi|abbr=on}} and ran at {{convert|15-20|km|mi|abbr=on}} for the rest.{{cite news |title=Metro rail completes biggest test trip so far |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/infrastructure/metro-rail-completes-trial-run-uttara-agargaon-342223 |access-date=4 December 2022 |work=The Business Standard |date=12 December 2021 |language=en}} == Overview == Line 6 consists of 16 elevated stations of 180m length each, and {{convert|20.1|km|mi|abbr=on}} of electricity-powered light rail tracks. All of line 6, save for the depot and some of its accompanying LRT, will be elevated above current roads. Mostly, this will be above road medians to allow traffic flow underneath, with stations also elevated. The Dhaka Metro is projected to serve more than 60,000 passengers per hour by 2022, with headways of approximately 4 minutes.{{Cite news |url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2014/09/23/dhaka-metrorail-to-carry-60000-people-per-hour|title=Dhaka Metrorail to carry 60,000 people per hour|last=Ahmed|first=Shamim|work=bdnews24.com|access-date=17 February 2019|archive-date=18 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218082054/https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2014/09/23/dhaka-metrorail-to-carry-60000-people-per-hour|url-status=live}} The entire route can be travelled in less than 40 minutes at a speed of {{convert|100|km/h|mph|abbr=on}}, and is expected to drastically reduce the number of private cars on Dhaka's streets as well as their potentially 7-hour-long standstills.{{Cite news |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/world/2012/12/22/traffic_chaos_reigns_in_bangladesh.html|title=Traffic chaos reigns in Bangladesh|work=The Star|language=en|access-date=17 February 2019|archive-date=15 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210615135932/https://www.thestar.com/news/world/2012/12/22/traffic_chaos_reigns_in_bangladesh.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.daily-sun.com/printversion/details/156973/Metro-rail-construction-in-progress|title=Metro rail construction in progress|work=Daily Sun|language=en|access-date=28 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202043414/http://www.daily-sun.com/printversion/details/156973/Metro-rail-construction-in-progress|url-status=live}} The system plans to use magnetic contactless Integrated Circuit Ticketing, commonly known as smart cards. [[Platform screen door]] (PSD) barriers used at the platform level will increase safety and increase efficiency. Trains of six spacious air-conditioned cars will arrive every four minutes going each way at each of the 16 stations. The project is being managed by the Communications Ministry's Dhaka Transport Co-ordination Authority, and a consortium of foreign and Bangladeshi firms known as the NKDM Association is acting as the project's general consultant. Other lines are being planned.{{cite web |title=At a Glance |url=http://dmtcl.gov.bd/site/page/ccdc49ad-c632-4953-bbce-acfdad3e830d/At-a-Glance-Dhaka-Mass-Transit-Company-Limited |website=dmtcl.gov.bd |access-date=1 December 2021 |language=en |archive-date=1 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211201151644/http://dmtcl.gov.bd/site/page/ccdc49ad-c632-4953-bbce-acfdad3e830d/At-a-Glance-Dhaka-Mass-Transit-Company-Limited |url-status=live }}}} ! colspan="2" style="text-align:right;" | ! ! |} {{Dhaka Metro}} ==Lines== ===MRT Line-1=== {{More|MRT Line 1 (Dhaka Metro)}} ====Airport Route==== The construction of the {{convert|19.872|km|mi|abbr=on}} long underground line, MRT Line-1 (Airport Route), is set to begin in December 2022, costing US$6.1 billion after many delays. Its deadline is set for 2026.{{cite news |title=Dhaka's first underground metro work begins in December |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/infrastructure/dhakas-first-underground-metro-work-begins-december-518526 |access-date=22 November 2022 |work=The Business Standard |date=23 October 2022 |language=en}} It will start from [[Shahjalal International Airport]] and stop at [[Kamalapur Railway Station]]. The line will have 12 underground stations. Stations will be constructed at [[Shahjalal International Airport]], [[Shahjalal International Airport|Shahjalal International Airport Terminal 3]], Khilkhet, Jamuna Future Park, Notun Bazar, Uttar Badda, Badda, Hatirjheel East, Rampura, Malibagh, Rajarbagh and Kamalapur Railway Station. MRT Line-1 will have an interchange of MRT Line-6, MRT Line-2 and MRT Line-4 at Kamalapur Railway Station. There will be interchange for the MRT Line-5 Northern Route and the MRT Line-1's Purbachal route at the Nutun Bazar. Hatirjheel East of MRT Line-1 and Aftab Nagar West Station of MRT Line-5: Southern Route will have Interchange. Above all, the airport will have an interchange of MRT Line-1 with BRT Line-3.{{cite web|title=DHAKA MASS TRANSIT COMPANY LIMITED (DMTCL)|url=http://dmtcl.gov.bd/site/page/a2655583-e801-451e-8208-c772c8f3eb25/-|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627220230/http://dmtcl.gov.bd/site/page/a2655583-e801-451e-8208-c772c8f3eb25/-|archive-date=27 June 2021|access-date=8 October 2021|website=dmtcl.gov.bd|language=en}} The government will provide US$1.5 billion while the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) will fund US$4.6 billion.{{cite news |title=Construction of Bangladesh's first underground metro line to begin March 2022 |url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/06/17/construction-of-bangladesh-s-first-metro-line-likely-to-begin-in-march-2022 |access-date=22 September 2021 |work=Dhaka Tribune |date=17 June 2021 |archive-date=21 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921223730/https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/06/17/construction-of-bangladesh-s-first-metro-line-likely-to-begin-in-march-2022 |url-status=live }} The use of soundless TBMs will make it possible to build MRT-1's underground infrastructure without disrupting the daily lives of residents and businesses. ====Purbachal Route==== MRT Line-1 (Purbachal Route) will be {{convert|11.369|km|mi|abbr=on}} long and it will have stations at Notun Bazar, Jamuna Future Park, Bashundhara, Police Officers’ Housing Society, Mastul, Purbachal West, Purbachal Centre, Purbachal Sector-7 and Purbachal depot. Of these stations, Notun Bazar and Jamuna Future Park would be underground as a part of the airport route. ===MRT Line-2=== {{Expand section|date=December 2021}} MRT Line-2 will connect Gabtali with Chittagong Road. The stations on this route are - Gabtali, Embankment Road, Basila, Mohammadpur, Lalmatia, Dhanmondi-27, Sat Masjid Road, Jigatola, Dhanmondi-2, Science Laboratory, Elephant Road, New Market, Nilkhet, BUET, Azimpur, Dhaka Medical College. Wari, Motijheel, Arambagh, Kamalapur Railway Station, Mugda, Manda, Demra and finally Chittagong Road. The length of this line will be {{convert|24|km|mi|abbr=on}}. It will cost about 3 billion dollars. ===MRT Line-4=== {{Expand section|date=December 2021}} MRT Line-4 will connect Kamalapur Railway Station with Narayanganj with underground lines. Length of this line will be {{convert|16|km|mi|abbr=on}}. According to a survey conducted by Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), MRT Line-4 will run parallel to an existing line which will be converted to a dual gauge railway line by the order of the Bangladesh Railway Authority. MRT Line-4 may not be financially viable.{{cite news |title=Big relief for commuters only after 2030 |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/transport/big-relief-commuters-only-after-2030-316015 |access-date=6 December 2021 |work=The Business Standard |date=14 October 2021 |language=en}} ===MRT Line-5 === ==== Northern Route ==== Construction of MRT Line-5 (Northern Route) will begin in June 2023.{{cite news |last1=Adhikary |first1=Tuhin Shubhra |title=Fast-Track Projects: Debt repayment a worry now |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/economy/national-budget/news/mega-projects-start-giving-dividends-3043891 |access-date=10 June 2022 |work=The Daily Star |date=10 June 2022 |language=en}} MRT Line-5 (Northern Route) will start from Hemayetpur of [[Savar Upazila]] and end at [[Vatara Thana|Bhatara]], costing US$4.85 billion.{{cite news |last1=Byron |first1=Rejaul Karim |last2=Adhikary |first2=Tuhin Shubhra |title=Dhaka Metro Rail: Two more lines to cost Tk 93,800cr |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/news/dhaka-metro-rail-two-more-lines-cost-tk-93800cr-1813843 |access-date=8 October 2021 |work=The Daily Star |date=15 October 2019 |language=en |archive-date=24 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200124052554/https://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/news/dhaka-metro-rail-two-more-lines-cost-tk-93800cr-1813843 |url-status=live }} It expected to be {{convert|20|km|mi|abbr=on}} long in total. Northern route will be {{convert|13.5|km|mi|abbr=on}} underground and {{convert|6.5|km|mi|abbr=on}} elevated. It will have 14 stations, of which 9 stations will be underground. Those underground stations will be constructed at Gabtoli, [[Darus Salam Thana|Darus Salam]], Mirpur 1, Mirpur 10, Mirpur 14, Kachukhet, Banani, Gulshan-2 and Notun Bazar. 5 stations will be elevated. 5 elevated stations will be constructed at Hemayetpur, Baliarpur, Bilamalia, Amin Bazar and Bhatara. MRT Line-5 (Northern Route) will have depot at Hemayetpur of [[Savar Upazila]].{{cite web |title=DHAKA MASS TRANSIT COMPANY LIMITED (DMTCL) |url=http://dmtcl.gov.bd/site/page/6e47d655-0c39-409a-bef5-a2d24063dfe3/- |website=dmtcl.gov.bd |access-date=8 October 2021 |language=en |archive-date=28 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628115614/http://dmtcl.gov.bd/site/page/6e47d655-0c39-409a-bef5-a2d24063dfe3/- |url-status=live }} ==== Southern Route ==== {{Expand section|date=December 2021}} The MRT Line-5 (Southern Route), which is about {{convert|17.4|km|mi|abbr=on}} long, is expected to be operational between 2027-2030. It will connect Gabtoli with Dasherkandi. The stations on this route are Gabtoli, Technical Circle, Kallyanpur, Shyamoli, College Gate, Asad Gate, Russell Square, West Panthapath, Karwan Bazar, Hatirjheel, Tejgaon, Niketon, Aftabnagar West, Aftabnagar Center, Aftabnagar East and lastly Dasherkandi. It is possible to interchange with MRT 5 (Northern Route). ===MRT Line-6=== {{See also|MRT Line 6 (Dhaka Metro)}} [[File:ঢাকা মেট্রোরেল By Showrov1007.jpg|thumb|Line 6]] [[MRT Line 6|MRT Line-6]] has 17 elevated stations each 180 meters long and {{convert|21.26|km|mi|abbr=on}} of electric light rail track (LRT). All Line-6 and some attending [[Light rapid transit|LRTs]], except the depot, have been elevated above the existing roads to allow traffic flow below. This line consists of three phases, of which only the first is currently operational. * Opened on 29 December 2022, from Uttara North to Agargaon. 11.73 kilometers (7.29 mi) * Slated for completion in December 2023, from Agargaon to Motijheel. 8.37 kilometers (5.20 mi) * Slated for completion in December 2025, from Motijheel to Kamalapur. 1.16 kilometers (0.72 mi) ==Service== ===Fare=== Fare chart
